name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'

jobs:
  tests:
    name: Tests on PHP ${{ matrix.php }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        php:
          - '8.3'
          - '8.4'
          - '8.5'
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: ${{ matrix.php }}
          extensions: dom, filter, iconv, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, phar, simplexml, tokenizer, xmlwriter
          coverage: none
          ini-values: zend.assertions=1

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: 'true'

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Run the tests
        run: composer test

  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: dom, filter, iconv, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, phar, simplexml, tokenizer, xmlwriter
          coverage: none

      - name: Validate the Composer manifest against the lock file
        run: composer validate --strict --no-check-publish

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: 'true'

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Check the formatting
        run: composer format:check

      - name: Analyse with PHPStan
        run: composer phpstan

      - name: Check PHP compatibility
        run: composer compat

      - name: Check the source metrics
        run: composer loc-guard

      - name: Check the directory structure
        run: composer tree-guard

      - name: Check the architecture layers
        run: composer deptrac

      - name: Keep ISO's artifacts between runs
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9
        with:
          path: build/iso
          key: iso-artifacts-${{ hashFiles('spec/iso/artifacts.txt') }}

      - name: Check the GQL specification
        run: composer spec

  mutation:
    name: Mutation testing
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: dom, filter, iconv, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, phar, simplexml, tokenizer, xmlwriter
          coverage: pcov
          ini-values: zend.assertions=1, memory_limit=1G
          tools: infection:0.35.4

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: 'true'

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Mutation testing on changed lines
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: >-
          php -d memory_limit=4G "$(command -v infection)"
          --configuration=infection.json5
          --threads=max
          --only-covering-test-cases
          --git-diff-lines
          --git-diff-base="origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}"
          --ignore-msi-with-no-mutations
          --min-msi=85
          --min-covered-msi=85
          --no-progress
          --logger-github

      - name: Mutation testing on the whole source tree
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: >-
          php -d memory_limit=4G "$(command -v infection)"
          --configuration=infection.json5
          --threads=max
          --only-covering-test-cases
          --no-progress
          --logger-github

      - name: Reject skipped whole-tree mutants
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          php -d memory_limit=1G -r '
            $report = json_decode(file_get_contents("build/infection/infection.json"), true, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
            if (($report["stats"]["skippedCount"] ?? null) !== 0) {
                fwrite(STDERR, "Infection did not report zero skipped mutants; check the report and timeout against test durations.\n");
                exit(1);
            }
          '

      - name: Upload mutation reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        with:
          name: mutation-reports
          path: build/infection/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  build:
    name: Build the distributed binary
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: [tests, lint]
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.4'
          extensions: dom, filter, iconv, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, phar, simplexml, tokenizer, xmlwriter
          coverage: none
          ini-values: phar.readonly=0

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: 'true'

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Compile the PHAR
        run: composer compile

      - name: Check the PHAR carries no static analyser
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          php -r '
            $phar = new Phar("dist/peq.phar");
            $carried = 0;
            foreach (new RecursiveIteratorIterator($phar) as $file) {
                if (str_contains((string) $file, "phpstan")) {
                    $carried++;
                }
            }
            if ($carried !== 0) {
                fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("The PHAR carries %d PHPStan files; it is meant to carry none.\n", $carried));
                exit(1);
            }
          '

      - name: Check the PHAR offers only the engines it carries
        run: |

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'

jobs:
  tests:
    name: Tests on PHP ${{ matrix.php }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        php:
          - '8.3'
          - '8.4'
          - '8.5'
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: ${{ matrix.php }}
          extensions: dom, filter, iconv, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, phar, simplexml, tokenizer, xmlwriter
          coverage: none
          ini-values: zend.assertions=1

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: 'true'

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Run the tests
        run: composer test

  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: dom, filter, iconv, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, phar, simplexml, tokenizer, xmlwriter
          coverage: none

      - name: Validate the Composer manifest against the lock file
        run: composer validate --strict --no-check-publish

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: 'true'

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Check the formatting
        run: composer format:check

      - name: Analyse with PHPStan
        run: composer phpstan

      - name: Check PHP compatibility
        run: composer compat

      - name: Check the source metrics
        run: composer loc-guard

      - name: Check the directory structure
        run: composer tree-guard

      - name: Check the architecture layers
        run: composer deptrac

      - name: Keep ISO's artifacts between runs
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9
        with:
          path: build/iso
          key: iso-artifacts-${{ hashFiles('spec/iso/artifacts.txt') }}

      - name: Check the GQL specification
        run: composer spec

  mutation:
    name: Mutation testing
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: dom, filter, iconv, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, phar, simplexml, tokenizer, xmlwriter
          coverage: pcov
          ini-values: zend.assertions=1, memory_limit=1G
          tools: infection:0.35.4

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: 'true'

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Mutation testing on changed lines
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: >-
          php -d memory_limit=4G "$(command -v infection)"
          --configuration=infection.json5
          --threads=max
          --only-covering-test-cases
          --git-diff-lines
          --git-diff-base="origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}"
          --ignore-msi-with-no-mutations
          --min-msi=85
          --min-covered-msi=85
          --no-progress
          --logger-github

      - name: Mutation testing on the whole source tree
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: >-
          php -d memory_limit=4G "$(command -v infection)"
          --configuration=infection.json5
          --threads=max
          --only-covering-test-cases
          --no-progress
          --logger-github

      - name: Reject skipped whole-tree mutants
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          php -d memory_limit=1G -r '
            $report = json_decode(file_get_contents("build/infection/infection.json"), true, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
            if (($report["stats"]["skippedCount"] ?? null) !== 0) {
                fwrite(STDERR, "Infection did not report zero skipped mutants; check the report and timeout against test durations.\n");
                exit(1);
            }
          '

      - name: Upload mutation reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        with:
          name: mutation-reports
          path: build/infection/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  build:
    name: Build the distributed binary
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: [tests, lint]
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.4'
          extensions: dom, filter, iconv, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, phar, simplexml, tokenizer, xmlwriter
          coverage: none
          ini-values: phar.readonly=0

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: 'true'

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Compile the PHAR
        run: composer compile

      - name: Check the PHAR carries no static analyser
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          php -r '
            $phar = new Phar("dist/peq.phar");
            $carried = 0;
            foreach (new RecursiveIteratorIterator($phar) as $file) {
                if (str_contains((string) $file, "phpstan")) {
                    $carried++;
                }
            }
            if ($carried !== 0) {
                fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("The PHAR carries %d PHPStan files; it is meant to carry none.\n", $carried));
                exit(1);
            }
          '

      - name: Check the PHAR offers only the engines it carries
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          ./dist/peq.phar --help inspect | grep -q -- '--type=TYPE *Analyzer type (native|debug)'

          if ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src --type=phpstan >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo 'The PHAR accepted an analyzer it does not carry.' >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Check the PHAR reads a source tree
        run: ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src -L 1 | grep -q 'App\\Analyzer\\Graph\\Graph::addEdge'

      - name: Check the PHAR writes every format it offers
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          ./dist/peq.phar --help inspect | grep -q -- '--output=OUTPUT *Output format (tree|json|dot|table|graph|mermaid)'

          ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src -L 1 --output=json \
            | php -r 'json_decode(stream_get_contents(STDIN), true, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);'

          ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src -L 1 --output=dot | grep -q '^digraph '

          ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src -L 1 --output=table | grep -q '| Depth | Symbol'

          ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src -L 1 --output=graph | grep -q '──▶ App\\Analyzer\\Graph\\Graph::addEdge'

          ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src -L 1 --output=mermaid | grep -q '^flowchart LR$'

      - name: Check the PHAR answers a GQL query
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          ./dist/peq.phar --help graph | grep -q -- '--type=TYPE *Analyzer type (native|debug)'

          ./dist/peq.phar graph 'MATCH (c:Class) WHERE c.id = "App\\Analyzer\\Graph\\Graph" RETURN c.id' src \
            | grep -q '| App\\Analyzer\\Graph\\Graph |'

      - name: Upload the PHAR
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        with:
          name: peq.phar
          path: dist/peq.phar

L82: # Command Line Options cite32†​ L83: 
L84: Besides general Symfony Console application command line options, Infection has its own ones.
L85: ### `--threads` or `-j` cite33†​ L86: 
L87: If you want to run tests for mutated code in parallel, set this to something > 1. It will dramatically speed up mutation process. Please note that if your tests somehow depends on each other or use database, this option can lead to failing tests which give many false-positives results.
L88: 
L89: To automatically detect the number of CPU cores, use `--threads=max`.
L90: 
L91: For Infection versions below `0.26.15`, you can detect the number of CPU cores depending on OS:
L92: shell
L93: 
L94:     `# on Linux
L95:     infection -j$(nproc)
L96: 
L97:     # on OSX
L98:     infection -j$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)`
L99: 
L100: > Running Infection with more threads does not necessarily lead to better performance. Consider benchmarking several numbers to find one that works best for your particular case.
L101: ### `--test-framework` cite34†​ L102: 
L103: This is a name of the Test Framework to use. Currently, Infection supports `PHPUnit`, `PhpSpec`, `Codeception` and `Testo`.
L104: 
L105: If you are using `infection/infection` Composer package, `PHPUnit` is installed by default. Other test framework adapters will be automatically installed on demand.
L106: cite35†PHAR distribution is bundled with all available adapters.
L107: 
L108: > Feel free to request a new test framework to be supported out of the box in GitHub’s issues.
L109: ### `--test-framework-extra-args` cite36†​ L110: 
L111: Available in Infection 0.34.0+
L112: 
L113: This option allows passing additional options and arguments to the test framework. Example for `PHPUnit`:
L114: 
L115: shell
L116: 
L117:     `infection --test-framework-extra-args="--verbose --filter=just/unit/tests"`
L118: 
L119: This will execute the `PHPUnit` as:
L120: 
L121: shell
L122: 
L123:     `phpunit [...infection options] --verbose --filter=just/unit/tests`
L124: 
L125: or, another example with argument: this will narrow executed tests only for 1 file:
L126: shell
L127: 
L128:     `infection --test-framework-extra-args="tests/FooTest.php"`
L129: 
L130: This will execute the `PHPUnit` as:
L131: 
L132: shell
L133: 
L134:     `phpunit [...infection options] tests/FooTest.php`
L135: > Please note that if you choose to use `--configuration`, `--filter`, or `--testsuite` for `PHPUnit`, these options will only be applied to the initial test run. Each mutation has a custom `phpunit.xml` file generated for it which defines a single testsuite containing the tests which should be executed for that mutation. Applying `--filter` or `--testsuite` would not make sense in this context as the tests have already been filtered down.
L136: ### `--test-framework-options` (deprecated) cite37†​ L137: 
L138: This option is deprecated since `0.34.0`.
L139: 
L140: Use cite36†`--test-framework-extra-args` instead.
L141: ### `--coverage` cite38†​ L142: 
L143: Path to the existing coverage reports.
L144: 
L145: When you use Continuous Integration for your project, probably you are already generating code coverage metrics and run `PHPUnit` with `Xdebug`/`phpdbg` enabled. Then, you run Infection for mutation testing, which in its turn, generates Code Coverage again for internal needs. This dramatically increases the build time because running your tests with debugger twice requires too much time.
L146: With this option it’s possible to reuse already generated coverage in Infection.
L147: 
L148: For `PHPUnit` and `Codeception`:
L149: 
L150:   * Infection requires both the`xml` and `junit` reports to work
L151:   * If `build/coverage` path is provided, it should contain `coverage-xml` folder and `junit.xml` file
L152:     * `build/coverage/coverage-xml/*`
L153:     * `build/coverage/junit.xml`
L154: 
L155: For `PhpSpec`:
L156: 
L157:   * Infection requires the `xml` report to work
L158:   * If `build/coverage` path is provided, it should contain `phpspec-coverage-xml` folder
L159: Example:
L160: 
L161: shell
L162: 
L163:     `# collect coverage
L164:     vendor/bin/phpunit --coverage-xml=build/coverage/coverage-xml --log-junit=build/coverage/junit.xml
L165: 
L166:     # use coverage
L167:     infection.phar --coverage=build/coverage`
L168: ### `--git-diff-filter` cite39†​ L169: 
L170: Allows filtering files to mutate by using `git diff` with `--diff-filter` option. Sensible values are: `AM` - added and modified files. `A` - only added files.
L171: 
L172: Best to be used during pull request builds on CI, e.g. with GitHub Actions, Travis CI and so on.
L173: 
L174: Usage:
L175: 
L176: shell
L177: 
L178:     `# this is needed on GitHub Actions to fetch the base branch to make a diff
L179:     git fetch --depth=1 origin $GITHUB_BASE_REF
L180: 
L181:     infection.phar --git-diff-filter=A`
L182: This command will mutate only those files that were added in the Pull Request. The diff is done between the current branch and a common ancestor of it and the base branch. If there is no common ancestor available, perhaps because your CI server used a shallow checkout, or you have unrelated branches, infection will use a direct diff between branches as a fallback.
L183: 
L184: > It’s possible to configure the base branch, see cite40†`--git-diff-base` option
L185: > It’s possible to mutate only touched lines, see cite41†`--git-diff-lines` option
L186: 
L187: You can check the result of the filter applied by using `infection config:list-sources` and/or debug the
L188: git values used by using the infection git commands. They can be listed with `infection list git`.
L189: ### `--git-diff-base` cite40†​ L190: 
L191: Supposed to be used only with cite39†`--git-diff-filter` option. Configures the base branch for `git diff` command.
L192: 
L193: Usage:
L194: 
L195: shell
L196: 
L197:     `# this is needed on GitHub Actions to fetch the base branch to make a diff
L198:     git fetch --depth=1 origin $GITHUB_BASE_REF
L199: 
L200:     infection.phar --git-diff-base=origin/$GITHUB_BASE_REF --git-diff-filter=AM`
L201: You can check the result of the filter applied by using `infection config:list-sources` and/or debug the
L202: git values used by using the infection git commands. They can be listed with `infection list git`.
L203: ### `--git-diff-lines` cite41†​ L204: 
L205: Allows mutating only touched lines of code. Under the hood, this option mutates only added and changed files, comparing your current branch with `master` branch by default.
L206: 
L207: Base branch can be changed by using `--git-diff-base=main` option. In this case, your current branch will be compared with `main` branch.
L208: Useful to check how your changes impacts MSI in a feature branch. Useful for those who do not want / can’t write tests for the whole touched legacy file, but wants to cover their own changes (only modified lines).
L209: 
L210: Can significantly improve performance since fewer Mutants are generated in comparison to using `--git-diff-filter=AM` or mutating all files.
L211: You can check the result of the filter applied by using `infection config:list-sources` and/or debug the
L212: git values used by using the infection git commands. They can be listed with `infection list git`.
L213: ### `--map-source-class-to-test` cite42†​ L214: 
L215: > Meant to be used together with `--git-diff-lines` / `--git-diff-filter` / `--filter`
L216: 
L217: This option can dramatically decrease the time needed for “Initial Tests Run” stage.
L218: If project has `N` tests files and we run Infection with, for example, `infection --git-diff-lines` and only 1 file `Foo.php` is updated/added in a Pull Request - it doesn’t make sense to run all the `N` tests to generate code coverage if we know that only 1 file of `N` covers the source code file - `FooTest.php`.
L219: 
L220: In practice, `PHPUnit` even has different methods that help define which test file covers which class:
L221:   * cite43†`requireCoverageMetadata`†docs.phpunit.de configuration attribute
L222:   * cite44†`#[CoversClass(...)]`†docs.phpunit.de attribute
L223: 
L224: In the example above, Infection would run only `FooTest.php` to generate coverage for `Foo.php`.
L225: 
L226: Without this option, Infection will attempt to run all the project’s tests, as it doesn’t know which tests cover `Foo.php`.
L227: Currently, `--map-source-class-to-test` supports the only one strategy of mapping source class to test file: by adding `*Test` postfix to a file name. If source class is named `Foo`, Infection will try to run `FooTest`.
L228: 
L229: Under the hood, it builds a regex for `--filter` option: `--filter='FooTest|BarTest'`.
L230: ### `--id` cite45†​ L231: 
L232: Available in Infection 0.30.0+
L233: 
L234: Run only one Mutant by its ID. Can be used multiple times. If source code is changed, this value can be invalidated. Pass all previous options with this one.
L235: 
L236: Example of usage: you completed a feature and wrote tests, then you run
L237: 
L238: shell
L239: 
L240:     `infection --git-diff-lines`
L241: 
L242: to get all mutations for the new and changed lines. But if there are too many mutations, it can be more convenient to focus on just 1 mutant at a time.
L243: Imagine you want to work on this Mutant:
L244: 
L245: diff
L246: 
L247:     `11) src/SourceClass.php:9    [M] Minus [ID] 6fa7eadad5b9fd1a72e4d80c83a61cc3
L248: 
L249:     @@ @@
L250:      {
L251:     -    public function hello(): string
L252:     +    protected function hello(): string
L253:          {
L254:              return 'hello';
L255:          }
L256:      }`
L257: 
L258: So you copy `6fa7eadad5b9fd1a72e4d80c83a61cc3` value and run the same command as previously, just adding `--id=6fa7eadad5b9fd1a72e4d80c83a61cc3`:
L259: shell
L260: 
L261:     `infection --git-diff-lines --id=6fa7eadad5b9fd1a72e4d80c83a61cc3`
L262: 
L263: With this, Infection will only produce one mutant, and you can update your tests and re-run this command to check if it’s killed or still not.
L264: ### `--logger-github` cite46†​ L265: 
L266: Supposed to be used only with GitHub Actions. This logger prints GitHub Annotation warnings for escaped Mutants right in the Pull Request.
L267: 
L268: Use `--logger-github=true` to force-enable or `--logger-github=false` to force-disable it.
L269: 
L270: Note that the GitHub Actions environment is automatically detected and this switch isn’t actually necessary when executed there.
L271: 
L272: cite47†Image: GitHub Annotation Escaped Mutant L273: 
L274: Usage:
L275: shell
L276: 
L277:     `# this is needed on GitHub Actions to fetch the base branch to make a diff
L278:     git fetch --depth=1 origin $GITHUB_BASE_REF
L279: 
L280:     infection.phar --logger-github --git-diff-filter=A`
L281: 
L282: Here is cite48†a real example†github.com how Infection uses it itself.
L283: 
L284: > Note: Infection automatically detects `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` environment variable for report linking.
L285: ### `--logger-gitlab` cite49†​ L286: 
L287: This option is used to provide a path to the generated GitLab (Code Climate) Code Quality Report:
L288: 
L289: shell
L290: 
L291:     `infection.phar --logger-gitlab='gitlab-coverage.json'`
L292: 
L293: After Infection completes its job, the `gitlab-coverage.json` file will be generated. This file can than be included as a `codequality` report artifact.
L294: Takes precedence over `logger.gitlab` setting inside `infection.json5` file. If you want to always generate the GitLab Coverage report it’s better to configure it inside `infection.json5`, see cite11†here .
L295: 
L296: > See cite50†this sample repository†gitlab.com as an example of how to configure Code Quality with Infection
L297: 
L298: This is how it works on PR main page:
L299: 
L300: cite51†Image: GitHub Annotation Escaped Mutant L301: 
L302: This is how it works on diff view:
L303: 
L304: cite52†Image: GitHub Annotation Escaped Mutant "}

L0: cite0†PHPUnit L1: 
L2: [Input: Search docs] [Input] [Input]
L3: 
L4: cite0†PHPUnit L5: # 2. Writing Tests for PHPUnitcite1† L6: 
L7: The tests for a class `Email` go into a class `EmailTest`. `EmailTest` inherits from `PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase`. The test methods are public methods that are named `test*`.
L8: 
L9: Alternatively, you can use the `PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Test` attribute on a method to mark it as a test method. See cite2†Test for details.
L10: Inside the test methods, assertion methods such as `assertSame()` (see cite3†Assertions ) are used to assert that an actual value matches an expected value.
L11: Example 2.1 A class named `Email` (declared in `src/Email.php`)cite4† L12: 
L13:     <?php declare(strict_types=1);
L14:     final class Email
L15:     {
L16:         private string $email;
L17: 
L18:         public static function fromString(string $email): self
L19:         {
L20:             return new self($email);
L21:         }
L22: 
L23:         private function __construct(string $email)
L24:         {
L25:             $this->ensureIsValidEmail($email);
L26: 
L27:             $this->email = $email;
L28:         }
L29: 
L30:         public function asString(): string
L31:         {
L32:             return $this->email;
L33:         }
L34: 
L35:         private function ensureIsValidEmail(string $email): void
L36:         {
L37:             if (!filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)) {
L38:                 throw new InvalidArgumentException(
L39:                     sprintf(
L40:                         '"%s" is not a valid email address',
L41:                         $email,
L42:                     ),
L43:                 );
L44:             }
L45:         }
L46:     }
L47: Example 2.2 A test class named `EmailTest` (declared in `tests/EmailTest.php`)cite5† L48: 
L49:     <?php declare(strict_types=1);
L50:     use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
L51: 
L52:     final class EmailTest extends TestCase
L53:     {
L54:         public function testCanBeCreatedFromValidEmail(): void
L55:         {
L56:             $string = 'user@example.org';
L57: 
L58:             $email = Email::fromString($string);
L59: 
L60:             $this->assertSame($string, $email->asString());
L61:         }
L62:         public function testCannotBeCreatedFromInvalidEmail(): void
L63:         {
L64:             $this->expectException(InvalidArgumentException::class);
L65: 
L66:             Email::fromString('invalid');
L67:         }
L68:     }
L69: Running the test shown above yields the output shown below:
L70: 
L71:     ./tools/phpunit tests/EmailTest.php
L72:     PHPUnit 12.5.34 by Sebastian Bergmann and contributors.
L73: 
L74:     Runtime:       PHP 8.5.10
L75: 
L76:     ..                                                                  2 / 2 (100%)
L77: 
L78:     Time: 00:00, Memory: 28.00 MB
L79: 
L80:     OK (2 tests, 2 assertions)
L81: 
L82: 
L83: The rest of this chapter uses `Email` and `EmailTest` to explain the fundamentals of writing tests for PHPUnit.
L84: ## Asserting return valuescite6† L85: 
L86: A test usually follows the “Arrange, Act, Assert” structure:
L87: 
L88:   * Arrange: Set up all necessary preconditions and inputs
L89: 
L90:   * Act: Perform the action under test
L91: 
L92:   * Assert: Verify that the expected results have occurred
L93: Let us look at `testCanBeCreatedFromValidEmail()` from the example shown above through the lens of “Arrange, Act, Assert”:
L94: 
L95:     public function testCanBeCreatedFromValidEmail(): void
L96:     {
L97:         // Arrange
L98:         $string = 'user@example.org';
L99: 
L100:         // Act
L101:         $email = Email::fromString($string);
L102: 
L103:         // Assert
L104:         $this->assertSame($string, $email->asString());
L105:     }
L106: 
L107: 
L108: The Arrange phase sets up the input: the string `'user@example.org'`.
L109: The Act phase calls `Email::fromString()` to create an `Email` object from this string.
L110: 
L111: The Assert phase uses `assertSame()` to verify that the `Email` object’s string representation matches the original input.
L112: 
L113: Asserting return values like this is the most common operation in a test method. See cite3†Assertions for the full list of assertion methods that PHPUnit provides.
L114: An assertion that fails ends the execution of the test method: the statements that follow the failed assertion, including any further assertions, are not executed. The first assertion that fails is therefore the only failure that is reported for a test.
L115: Example 2.3 A test method with three assertions, the second of which failscite7† L116: 
L117:     <?php declare(strict_types=1);
L118:     use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
L119: 
L120:     final class FailedAssertionTest extends TestCase
L121:     {
L122:         public function testAssertionsAfterAFailedAssertionAreNotExecuted(): void
L123:         {
L124:             $this->assertSame(1, 1);
L125:             $this->assertSame(2, 3);
L126:             $this->assertSame(4, 5);
L127:         }
L128:     }
L129: Running the test shown above yields the output shown below:
L130: 
L131:     ./tools/phpunit tests/FailedAssertionTest.php
L132:     PHPUnit 12.5.34 by Sebastian Bergmann and contributors.
L133: 
L134:     Runtime:       PHP 8.5.10
L135: 
L136:     F                                                                   1 / 1 (100%)
L137: 
L138:     Time: 00:00, Memory: 26.00 MB
L139: 
L140:     There was 1 failure:
L141: 
L142:     1) FailedAssertionTest::testAssertionsAfterAFailedAssertionAreNotExecuted
L143:     Failed asserting that 3 is identical to 2.
L144:     /path/to/tests/FailedAssertionTest.php:9
L145: 
L146:     FAILURES!
L147:     Tests: 1, Assertions: 2, Failures: 1.
L148: Only two assertions are counted: the third one was never executed.
L149: 
L150: Note
L151: 
L152: When you want to verify multiple values that belong together, assert the data structure as a whole using a single assertion instead of asserting each value separately. The failure of such an assertion shows all values that differ from what was expected, not just the first one.
L153: When you want each value to be verified and reported independently, use a cite8†data provider . Each data set is reported as a separate test, so the failure of one does not hide the result of another.
L154: Ideally, each test method should only verify one aspect of the system under test. In `testCanBeCreatedFromValidEmail()`, however, we technically test two things: that an `Email` object can be constructed from a valid string (the named constructor does not throw an exception and we do get an `Email` object) and that `asString()` returns the string representation of the `Email` value object. This is a typical deviation from the norm when testing the happy path of a constructor.
L155: The happy path is the scenario where everything works as expected: valid input is provided and the system behaves correctly. Its opposite is the unhappy path (also called the error path): the scenario where something goes wrong, for instance when invalid input is provided and an exception is expected. Testing the happy path of a constructor often involves verifying both that the object is created successfully and that it holds the expected state.
L156: ## Expecting exceptionscite9† L157: 
L158: When you expect an action to raise an exception, the test follows the “Arrange, Expect, Act” structure. The assertion (expectation) is set up before the action that is expected to throw the exception.
L159: Let us look at `testCannotBeCreatedFromInvalidEmail()` from the example shown above through the lens of “Arrange, Expect, Act”:
L160: 
L161:     public function testCannotBeCreatedFromInvalidEmail(): void
L162:     {
L163:         // Expect
L164:         $this->expectException(InvalidArgumentException::class);
L165: 
L166:         // Act
L167:         Email::fromString('invalid');
L168:     }
L169: 
L170: 
L171: The Expect phase tells PHPUnit that the code is expected to throw an `InvalidArgumentException`.
L172: The Act phase calls `Email::fromString()` with an invalid email address. If the expected exception is not thrown, the test fails.
L173: 
L174: The `expectException()` method must be called before the code that is expected to throw the exception. This is why the structure is “Arrange, Expect, Act” and not “Arrange, Act, Assert”.
L175: In addition to the `expectException()` method, the `expectExceptionCode()`, `expectExceptionMessage()`, and `expectExceptionMessageMatches()` methods exist to set up expectations for exceptions raised by the code under test.
L176: 
L177: Note
L178: 
L179: Note that `expectExceptionMessage()` asserts that the `$actual` message contains the `$expected` message and does not perform an exact string comparison.
L180: The `expectExceptionObject(Throwable $exception)` method can be used to set up expectations for the class, the message, and the code of an exception based on an example object:
L181: 
L182:     $this->expectExceptionObject(new InvalidArgumentException('message', 1));
L183: 
L184: 
L185: The call shown above is equivalent to the three calls shown below:
L186: 
L187:     $this->expectException(InvalidArgumentException::class);
L188:     $this->expectExceptionMessage('message');
L189:     $this->expectExceptionCode(1);
L190: ## Verifying side effectscite10† L191: 
L192: Not everything that needs testing is a return value or an exception. A method may have side effects: it may call a method on a collaborating object or perform an I/O operation such as writing to a database or to the filesystem.
L193: 
L194: Sometimes the system under test depends on values returned by a collaborating object. Test Stubs allow you to control these indirect inputs.
L195: Sometimes you need to verify that the system under test calls a method on a collaborating object with the expected arguments. Mock Objects allow you to verify these indirect outputs.
L196: 
L197: Test Stubs and Mock Objects are discussed in detail in the chapter on cite11†Test Doubles .
L198: ## Data Providerscite12† L199: 
L200: A test method can accept arbitrary arguments. These arguments are to be provided by one or more data provider methods (`additionProvider()` in the example shown below). The data provider method to be used is specified using the `PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider` attribute.
L201: A data provider method must be `public` and `static` and its name must not start with `test`. It must return a value that is cite13†iterable†www.php.net , either an array or an object that implements the `Traversable` interface. In each iteration step, it must yield an array. For each of these arrays, the test method will be called with the contents of the array as its arguments.
L202: Example 2.4 Using a data provider that returns an array of arrayscite14† L203: 
L204:     <?php declare(strict_types=1);
L205:     use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
L206:     use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
L207: 
L208:     final class NumericDataSetsTest extends TestCase
L209:     {
L210:         public static function additionProvider(): array
L211:         {
L212:             return [
L213:                 [0, 0, 0],
L214:                 [0, 1, 1],
L215:                 [1, 0, 1],
L216:                 [1, 1, 3],
L217:             ];
L218:         }
L219:         #[DataProvider('additionProvider')]
L220:         public function testAdd(int $a, int $b, int $expected): void
L221:         {
L222:             $this->assertSame($expected, $a + $b);
L223:         }
L224:     }
L225: Running the test shown above yields the output shown below:
L226: 
L227:     ./tools/phpunit tests/NumericDataSetsTest.php
L228:     PHPUnit 12.5.34 by Sebastian Bergmann and contributors.
L229: 
L230:     Runtime:       PHP 8.5.10
L231: 
L232:     ...F                                                                4 / 4 (100%)
L233: 
L234:     Time: 00:00, Memory: 28.00 MB
L235: 
L236:     There was 1 failure:
L237: 
L238:     1) NumericDataSetsTest::testAdd#3 with data (1, 1, 3)
L239:     Failed asserting that 2 is identical to 3.
L240:     /path/to/tests/NumericDataSetsTest.php:20
L241: 
L242:     FAILURES!
L243:     Tests: 4, Assertions: 4, Failures: 1.
L244: It is useful to name each data set with a string key. Output will be more verbose as it will contain the name of the data set that breaks a test.
L245: Example 2.5 Using a data provider with named data setscite15† L246: 
L247:     <?php declare(strict_types=1);
L248:     use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
L249:     use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
L250: 
L251:     final class NamedDataSetsTest extends TestCase
L252:     {
L253:         public static function additionProvider(): array
L254:         {
L255:             return [
L256:                 'adding zeros'  => [0, 0, 0],
L257:                 'zero plus one' => [0, 1, 1],
L258:                 'one plus zero' => [1, 0, 1],
L259:                 'one plus one'  => [1, 1, 3],
L260:             ];
L261:         }
L262: 
L263:         #[DataProvider('additionProvider')]
L264:         public function testAdd(int $a, int $b, int $expected): void
L265:         {
L266:             $this->assertSame($expected, $a + $b);
L267:         }
L268:     }
L269: Running the test shown above yields the output shown below:
L270: 
L271:     ./tools/phpunit tests/NamedDataSetsTest.php
L272:     PHPUnit 12.5.34 by Sebastian Bergmann and contributors.
L273: 
L274:     Runtime:       PHP 8.5.10
L275: 
L276:     ...F                                                                4 / 4 (100%)
L277: 
L278:     Time: 00:00, Memory: 28.00 MB
L279: 
L280:     There was 1 failure:
L281: 
L282:     1) NamedDataSetsTest::testAdd@one plus one with data (1, 1, 3)
L283:     Failed asserting that 2 is identical to 3.
L284:     /path/to/tests/NamedDataSetsTest.php:20
L285: 
L286:     FAILURES!
L287:     Tests: 4, Assertions: 4, Failures: 1.
L288: Note
L289: 
L290: You can make the test output more verbose by defining a sentence and using the test’s parameter names as placeholders (`$a`, `$b` and `$expected` in the example above) with the cite16†TestDox attribute. You can also refer to the name of a named data set with `$_dataName`.
L291: 
L292: Individual data sets can be selected from the command line via the `--filter` option; see cite17†Filtering by test name for the syntax.
"}
